questions.question: How does Flexbox work and what are its main properties?
questions.title: Flexbox Basics
questions.direct_answer: Flexbox lays out children along one axis. On the container: display:flex activates it, flex-direction sets the axis (row/column), justify-content aligns along the main axis, align-items aligns on the cross axis, gap spaces children, flex-wrap allows wrapping. On children: flex-grow (share of free space), flex-shrink (how much it gives up when tight), flex-basis (starting size before growing), and the shorthand flex: 1 = 1 1 0. Use it for one-dimensional distribution: navbars, toolbars, card rows, centering.

Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C[display: flex] --> D[flex-direction: row]
    D --> MA[main axis: horizontal]
    D --> CA[cross axis: vertical]
    MA --> J[justify-content: start center space-between space-around space-evenly]
    CA --> A[align-items: stretch center flex-start flex-end baseline]
    I[flex item] --> G[flex-grow: share of free space]
    I --> S[flex-shrink: gives back when tight]
    I --> B[flex-basis: starting size]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The sizing algorithm (the mechanism worth knowing): flex computes in passes — first basis (each item's hypothetical size from flex-basis or content), then resolve violations: if total < container, POSITIVE free space is distributed by grow ratios; if total > container, NEGATIVE space is extracted weighted by shrink × basis (the basis weighting is the subtlety — a wide item shrinks more than a narrow one at the same flex-shrink). min-width: auto (the default) floors how far an item can shrink — the reason a long word or image won't compress past its min-content size and instead overflows the container.

flex-basis vs width (the confusion to resolve): basis is the STARTING size flex negotiates from; width is a hard declaration. In a flex context, basis overrides width for the main-axis sizing (that's why flex: 1 with basis 0 ignores content width for distribution). When people 'unset' flexbox sizing they set flex-basis: auto to return to content sizing.

The centering completeness (the flex answers everything follow-up): one-line centering (justify + align), plus margin: auto on a flex item absorbs ALL free space on the main axis — the pattern for footers pinned to the bottom of a card body. Flexbox also solved vertical centering that pre-2015 CSS needed hacks for (negative margins, tables, absolute + transform) — worth one sentence of history: this is why 'how do you center a div' stopped being a joke only recently.
